title: Relationship Pricing Grading Table: The Relationship Figure on a Certificate of Deposit Term
content:
The relationship figure earned on a new term of a certificate of the Certificates of Deposit line is graded by the checking account the owner holds and by how busy that account has been.

## 1. The grades

The relationship figure is graded: an owner who holds an active Premier Checking or Private Client Checking account on the day the new term is recorded and has had at least 6 deposits posted to that account in the three months before that day earns the tier's relationship bonus points in full; an owner who holds an active checking account of a tier the certificate's own tier lists as qualifying and has had fewer than 6 deposits posted to it in those three months earns three quarters of the tier's relationship bonus points; every other owner earns nothing, whatever checking account they hold and however many deposits were posted to it.

## 2. The same grades tabulated

| Active checking account held on the day the new term is recorded | Deposits posted to it in the three months before that day | Relationship figure earned |
|---|---|---|
| Premier Checking or Private Client Checking | 6 or more | the tier's relationship bonus points in full |
| Premier Checking or Private Client Checking | fewer than 6 | three quarters of the tier's relationship bonus points |
| a checking account of another tier the certificate's own tier lists as qualifying | fewer than 6 | three quarters of the tier's relationship bonus points |
| every other case | any number | nothing |

The accounts named are tiers of the bank's Personal Checking line, and the deposits counted are the deposits posted to that account, read from its own ledger over the three months ending on the day the new term is recorded.

## 3. Points of judgement

The count of 6 is a floor: exactly 6 deposits in the three months is "at least 6", so a Premier Checking holder with 6 deposits earns the points in full, and one with 5 earns three quarters of them.

The two upper grades ask different questions of the account's tier, and each also asks its own question of the deposit count. The full figure is confined to Premier Checking and Private Client Checking by name, and to accounts with 6 or more deposits. The three-quarter figure turns instead on the list of qualifying checking tiers the certificate's own tier publishes, and it asks for fewer than 6 deposits; so on a certificate whose tier lists Interest Checking as qualifying, an owner holding an active Interest Checking account with fewer than 6 deposits earns three quarters of the points.

An account can therefore fall outside both upper grades on either count. An active checking account of a tier the certificate's own tier does not list as qualifying reaches neither grade, whatever has been posted to it. An active Interest Checking account with 6 or more deposits also reaches neither: it is not one of the two tiers the full figure names, and the three-quarter figure asks for fewer than 6.

## 4. Worked readings, on hypothetical figures

Suppose the certificate's tier publishes relationship bonus points of 0.20 and lists Interest Checking, Premier Checking and Private Client Checking as qualifying.

| Owner's holding | Deposits in the three months | Figure earned |
|---|---|---|
| active Private Client Checking | 9 | 0.20 points |
| active Premier Checking | 2 | 0.15 points, being three quarters of 0.20 |
| active Interest Checking | 3 | 0.15 points, being three quarters of 0.20 |
| active Interest Checking | 11 | nothing |
| active Everyday Checking | 14 | nothing |
| no active checking account | none | nothing |

The two Interest Checking rows repay attention. The busier of the two accounts earns less, not more: the full figure is reserved to the two tiers named in the first grade, and the three-quarter figure is reserved to accounts with fewer than 6 deposits, so an active Interest Checking account with 11 deposits meets neither.
